newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba seeks to curb U.S. flag clothes fashion.
newsitem.headline: Cuba seeks to curb U.S. flag clothes fashion.

text.p: In Havana, the stars-and-stripes are officially a fashion "don't."

Cuba's official Union of Young Communists (UJC), citing the threat of "mental colonisation," is waging a campaign to persuade young Cubans not to sport clothes bearing the flag of the United States, a Cuban newspaper reported on Sunday.

The weekly Juventud Rebelde said the increasing use of clothes emblazoned with the U.S. flag was a major point of discussion at meetings held in Havana by local leaders of the UJC, the youth wing of Cuba's ruling Communist party.

"It was clear that this fashion was just the tip of the iceberg, which, beneath the surface, conceals a tangle of ideological contradictions and conflicts, which must be addressed to draw up and direct a conscious strategy of cultural resistance," the newspaper said, reporting on the discussion at the meetings.

Young Cubans can quite frequently be seen wearing jeans, T- shirts, caps or other clothes carrying the flag of the United States. The clothes are often sent by relatives and friends living in the United States.

The U.S. government has a longstanding political dispute with Cuba's communist rulers. Washington and Havana do not have formal diplomatic relations and the U.S. has tightened a 35-year-old economic embargo against the Caribbean island.
Juventud Rebelde quoted one member of the UJC's National Bureau, Enith Alerm, as saying that the wearing of clothes carrying the U.S. national emblem was a "manifestation of mental colonisation."

"Our battle is not just against the uncritical use of this symbol, but against U.S. domination, which is something much more extensive and shows itself in different ways," Alerm added. But she urged youth leaders to use persuasion and "our historical arguments" to act against the U.S. flag clothes fashion.
